fr:title.text: Notation: fields, groups, and the nilpotent geometry

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: Notation: fields, groups, and the nilpotent geometry

fr:mainmatter.html:p: The ambient objects, shared by both halves of the program (height and growth). Spellings agree with notes/steenrod-hsop.tex so that prose moves between journal and forest without retyping.

html:ul.html:li: \FF \mathbb {F}, \Fq \mathbb {F}_q, \Fqpow{m} \mathbb {F}_{q^{m}} — the base field and the layers of a Frobenius tower.
\PP \mathbb {P} — projective space; the pencil parameter lives on \mathbb {P}^1.

\powerseries{k}{u} k\lbrack \lbrack u \rbrack \rbrack and \laurent{k}{u} k\lbrack \lbrack u \rbrack \rbrack \lbrack u^{-1} \rbrack — the germ apparatus's coefficient rings. These must go through the macro: a literal double bracket inside math is read by the lexer as a wiki-link and aborts the build, whereas the macro spells the brackets as \lbrack and \rbrack control sequences, which the lexer never sees as brackets at all.

fr:mainmatter.html:p: Matrices and groups. The conjugation action of the unit group on the matrix algebra is the whole subject, so these are the most frequently used names in the forest.

html:ul.html:li: \Mat \mathrm {M}_n, \GL \mathrm {GL}_n, \PGL \mathrm {PGL}_n, \gl \mathfrak {gl}_n — matrix algebra, its unit group, the effective quotient, and the Lie algebra. Left unsubscripted so the subscript is written where it is meant.
\Borel B, \Levi L — the Borel subgroup and a Levi factor.
\Unitri U, \Unitrin{n} U_{n}, \Unitriq{n} U_{n}(\mathbb {F}_q) — the unitriangular group, abstractly and over the base field. Use the q-decorated form wherever the count depends on it.
\Nil \mathcal {N} — the nilpotent cone.
\orbit{\lambda} \mathcal {O}_{\lambda } — the nilpotent orbit of Jordan type \lambda \vdash n. \Orb \mathcal {O} is the bare letter, for when the type is carried some other way.
\FlagLocus \mathcal {FL} — the flag locus: the union of the k-rational nilradical conjugates. These are the witnesses that make the height bound sharp.

\nn \mathfrak {n} — a fixed nilradical (Borel or parabolic); \nilrad{c} \mathfrak {n}_{c} — the block-upper-triangular nilradical of the composition c. Note \mathfrak {n}_{n} (a composition with one part) is the full Borel nilradical.
\uu \mathfrak {u}, \parab \mathfrak {p}, \levi \mathfrak {l} — upper nilpotent, parabolic, Levi.
\centr{y} \mathfrak {z}(y) — the centralizer of y. The two graded counts cut out of it are named in the growth notation node.

fr:mainmatter.html:p: Operators. All spelled with \operatorname so that spacing is right and so that no undefined control sequence reaches the math renderer.

html:ul.html:li: \operatorname {tr}, \operatorname {rank}, \operatorname {span}, \operatorname {codim} — trace, rank, span, codimension.
\operatorname {ad}, \operatorname {Ad} — the adjoint actions of the Lie algebra and of the group.
\operatorname {Hom}, \operatorname {End}, \operatorname {Stab}, \operatorname {Ann}, \operatorname {soc}, \operatorname {res} — used in the extension-module ledger of the frontier.
\rig{\Xi} \operatorname {rig}(\Xi ) — the rigidity operator of the S_0-calculus.

fr:mainmatter.html:p: Every content tree opens with \import{preamble}, which pulls in the seven notation nodes below. Nothing else in the forest may define a macro: notation is fixed here, and a node that wants a new name adds it here first.

The point is not brevity. A concept that occurs in more than one node gets a name, and that name expands to the notation — so changing the notation is one edit, and two nodes cannot silently disagree about what a symbol means. Where a tree still writes raw \mathfrak {...} or \operatorname {...}, that is a concept the notation layer has not yet caught up with.

Text-level macros. None of them may appear inside math: they expand to forester prims, and the TeX-like printer refuses to serialize a prim, so a single one of these inside a math group aborts the whole build.
Inline emphasis. LaTeX-spelling aliases for the forester prims, kept so that prose transplanted from the journal builds unchanged.

html:ul.html:li: \textbf{...} — alias for \strong.
\emph{...} — alias for \em.
\term{...} — a term at its point of definition. Spelled the same as \emph today; kept separate so the two can diverge.

fr:mainmatter.html:p: Headed paragraphs. Every statement node in this forest is a short sequence of headed paragraphs. The heading is part of the node's meaning, not its styling, so it gets a macro: renaming the convention is then a single edit here rather than a sweep over seventeen trees.

html:ul.html:li: \statement{Theorem (H1).}{...} — a named statement; \headed is the same macro under a neutral name, for headings that are not statements; \lead{...} is the heading alone, for when a list rather than a paragraph follows.

\status{...}, \mechanism{...}, \consequence{...}, \remains{...}, \role{...} — the five recurring paragraph roles: what is known, why it is true, what it buys, what is still owed, where it sits in the skeleton.
\machine{...} — the machine record: logs, certificates and instrument names that back the claim.
\caution{...} — a live hazard, e.g. an instrument that is committed in a broken state.
\provenance{...} — the closing provenance line pointing into the journal and the experiment record. Every statement node ends with one.

\uses{[[ffi-0016]], [[ffi-0021]]} — the dependency line. This is the only thing that builds the citation graph: forester derives backlinks from links, not from \import, so a result that is used but not linked is invisible to the graph. Until proof nodes exist, this line is what a Stacks-style proof's inline citations would otherwise carry. ./check-dag.py verifies it.
\supersededby{[[...]]} — for a statement kept on the record because it was refuted or restated.

fr:title.text: Notation: Steenrod operations, the ideal J, and height

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: Notation: Steenrod operations, the ideal J, and height

fr:mainmatter.html:p: The height half of the program: the q-Steenrod operations, the ideal they generate, and the two dimension constants that every statement about it compares.

html:ul.html:li: \sP \mathcal {P} — the total operation \mathcal {P} \colon S \to S[T], x \mapsto x + x^q T on linear forms.
\Steen{i} \mathcal {P}^{i} — the i-th graded piece; \Steenof{i}{c_j} \mathcal {P}^{i}(c_j) — applied to an invariant. These are the generators of the ideal.
\Fr F, \Frob{M} F(M) — the entrywise Frobenius on \mathrm {M}_n(K). Note the clash flagged in the preamble node: the growth program writes F for an unrelated functional.

html:p.html:strong: The characteristic polynomial and its coefficients.

html:ul.html:li: \charpoly{X} \chi _{X} — the characteristic polynomial of the generic matrix.
\chcoef{j} c_{j} — its coefficients, the generators of S^G; c_{1} = \operatorname {tr} X and c_{n} = \det X.
\Jideal J — the Steenrod ideal; \Vloc{\Jideal} V(J) — its zero locus, the partner variety.
\height{\Jideal} \operatorname {ht} J — the height, with \hgt \operatorname {ht} the bare operator.

\conjht{n} \frac {n(n+1)}{2} — the conjectured height, equal to the number of generators; and \flagdim{n} \frac {n(n - 1)}{2} — the dimension of the flag locus, equal to the conjectured \dim V(J). Both take the rank as an argument, so they compose: the n = 9 row of the ladder is \frac {9(9+1)}{2} against \frac {9(9 - 1)}{2}.
\hsop expands to the words homogeneous system of parameters — used often enough in prose to be worth fixing once.

fr:mainmatter.html:p: Polarizations. The bihomogeneous pieces of c_{j}(sX + tY), from which the sparse trace-form generators are read off.

html:ul.html:li: \polar{a}{b} P_{a,b}, with P_{j,0} = c_{j}(X) and P_{0,j} = c_{j}(Y).

fr:title.text: Notation: the trace form and the symplectic skeleton

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: Notation: the trace form and the symplectic skeleton

fr:mainmatter.html:p: The apparatus common to the three avatars: the trace form, the Kostant--Kirillov form it induces on orbits, and the pencil-side objects that carry the same isotropy statement one scale down.

html:ul.html:li: \traceform{A}{B} \kappa (A, B) — the trace form on \mathfrak {gl}_n: perfect over every ring, symmetric, invariant. Its alternation \kappa ([P, A], A) = 0 is the source of every symplectic structure in the program.
\KK \omega — the Kostant--Kirillov form on a nilpotent orbit, in every characteristic.

fr:mainmatter.html:p: Orbit dimensions. The three recurring numbers of the program, all read off the partition.

html:ul.html:li: \centdim{\lambda} c(\lambda ) — the centralizer dimension c(\lambda ) = \sum _j (\lambda '_j)^2, the same in every characteristic.

\orbdim{\lambda} \dim \mathcal {O}_{\lambda } = n^2 - c(\lambda ), and \dim \mathrm {Fl}_{\lambda '} = \frac {1}{2}\dim \mathcal {O}_{\lambda }: every bound the program needs is half of an orbit dimension.

fr:mainmatter.html:p: Pencils. The objects of avatar 2.

html:ul.html:li:
\pencil{\mu}{
u}{N}{M} \mu N + 
u M — a nilpotent pencil: a matrix of linear forms over K[\mu , 
u ], every member nilpotent. \gentype 	au is its generic Jordan type.
\structsheaf \mathcal {O} — the structure sheaf. Note the clash flagged in the preamble node: \Orb prints the same glyph.

fr:title.text: Notation: class counts, modality, and the thread algebra

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: Notation: class counts, modality, and the thread algebra

fr:mainmatter.html:p: The growth half of the program: Higman's count, the three modalities that bound it, and the graded data of a generic centralizer that computes them.

html:ul.html:li: \classes{G} \kappa (G) — the number of conjugacy classes. \kU{n} \kappa (U_{n}) and \kUq{n} \kappa (U_{n}(\mathbb {F}_q)) are the unitriangular cases; use the q-decorated form when the dependence on q is the point.
\degkU{n} \deg \kappa (U_{n}) and \lckU{n} \operatorname {lc} \kappa (U_{n}) — degree and leading coefficient, defined wherever Higman's conjecture is known.

fr:mainmatter.html:p: The three modalities. Distinguished carefully: they are different invariants and the bridge theorem is precisely a comparison between them.

html:ul.html:li: \umod{W} \operatorname {umod}(W) — the U-modality of a U-stable irreducible W: \operatorname {umod}(W) = \dim W - \max _{y \in W} \dim U \cdot y, the dimension of the generic-orbit space.
\Bmodn{n} \operatorname {mod}(B : \mathfrak {n}_{n}) — the Borel modality on the full nilradical, the invariant the height program and the growth program share.
\modality{Q}{V} \operatorname {mod}(Q : V) — the general form, for a parabolic or reductive Q acting on V; \Bmod{V} \operatorname {mod}(B : V) fixes Q = B.
\umodop \operatorname {umod} and \modop \operatorname {mod} — the bare operators, for the places where the argument is carried in an exponent rather than in parentheses.

fr:mainmatter.html:p: The two closed forms. These are the arithmetic content of the degree and leading-term laws, and they occur in nearly every growth node; both take the rank as an argument.

html:ul.html:li: \degfloor{n} \lfloor n(n+6)/12 \rfloor — the degree law's value, and the exponent in the growth theorem's lower bound.
\lcvalue{n} n / \gcd (n, 6) — the conjectured leading coefficient for n \ge 8.
\Munimodal{n} M_{\mathrm {unimodal}}(n) — the argmax count of the grand formula over unimodal compositions, the proven half of the leading-term law.

fr:mainmatter.html:p: The thread algebra and the graded centralizer counts. This is the machinery the grand formula is proved with.

html:ul.html:li: \zu{c} z_u(c) — the dimension of \mathfrak {z}(y) \cap \mathfrak {u} for y \in \mathfrak {n}_{c} generic; and \zq{y} z_q(y) — its reductive-repair companion, which the Q-fibration shows equal to it.

\Ncount{k}{c} N_{k}(c) — the degree-k graded count, and \ezero{c} e_0(c) — the degree-zero defect, so that z_u(c) = \sum _{k \ge 1} N_{k}(c) + e_0(c). That e_0(c) \ge 0 is the load-bearing exactness statement.
\thread \mathfrak {s} — the thread algebra, the Levi projection of the graded centralizer; e_0(c) is measured inside it.

\wallpen \sum \Delta ^2 — the wall penalty, over consecutive jumps of the zero-padded profile; \Ffun \frac {1}{2}\bigl [n + \sum _i c_i^2 - \sum \Delta ^2\bigr ] — the functional F it sits in, and \Fof{c} F(c) the same functional named at an argument.

fr:title.text: Notation: splits, flanks, and the Fredholm ledger

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: Notation: splits, flanks, and the Fredholm ledger

fr:mainmatter.html:p: The vocabulary of the current frontier: splitting a composition about its longest block, and the four counts whose comparison is the whole remaining content of multi-block Lemma V.

html:ul.html:li: \splitc{\flankL}{v}{\flankR} (c_L, v, c_R) — a split of a composition, isolating a middle block of size v with flanks \flankL c_L and \flankR c_R. The split is tall when \max (c_L) \ge v and \max (c_R) \ge v.
\Ltil \widetilde {L}, \Rtil \widetilde {R} — the flanks with the v longest parts incremented, the modules the extension ledger is computed in.
\quotdata c' — the reductive quotient datum of a split; also the canonical unimodalization of a composition.

fr:mainmatter.html:p: The Fredholm ledger. Four counts; the frontier is a single inequality between two of them.

html:ul.html:li: The ledger is exact: N_{\mathrm {weak}} \le N_z + \binom {v+1}{2} is equivalent to Lemma V, and N_{\mathrm {weak}} \le N_{\mathrm {strict}} + \binom {v+1}{2} is automatic — so the open statement is N_{\mathrm {strict}} \le N_z.

fr:mainmatter.html:p: The peeling induction. One peel of a flank, and the two local comparisons it must preserve.

html:ul.html:li: \excess{s} \mathrm {ex}_{s}, \excess{z} \mathrm {ex}_{z} — the excess terms of the exact one-peel ladders, capped by \operatorname {codim} \operatorname {res} B; \qterm{s} q_{s}, \qterm{z} q_{z} — the quotient terms. The two comparisons the induction needs are \mathrm {ex}_{s} \le \mathrm {ex}_{z} and q_{s} \le q_{z}.
\Szero S_0, \Szeros S_0^{s} — the rigidity sets, with S_0^{s} \subseteq S_0 always; the first comparison is equivalent to S_0 \subseteq S_0^{s} + \operatorname {res} B.
\resB \operatorname {res} B — the restriction image the peel factors through.

fr:title.text: Notation: names of the standing statements

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: Notation: names of the standing statements

fr:mainmatter.html:p: The program refers to its own results by tag — (H1), (W), (M8) — far more often than by statement. Those tags are notation and belong here, so that a rename is one edit and so that no node invents a variant spelling.
These are prose-only. Inside math a tag would be set as juxtaposed italic variables, so put it outside the math group rather than inside — ./check-math.py fails the build record if one slips in.

html:ul.html:li: \Hone (H1) — the incidence theorem for flagless pencils. Proven.
\starred (*) — the characteristic-p subvariety inference: the sole open content of the height conjecture after (H1).
\Meight (M8) — the per-cell modality reduction that closes n = 8; \Sred (S) and \Splus (S+) — the reduction and the ledger conjecture that close n = 9.
\Wallone Wall 1 — the coisotropy of the cyclic cocycle on the survivor algebra.
\Wconj (W) — the infinitesimal avatar of (*); \anomalylaw (anomaly law) — which germs it fails at.
\NSconj (NS) — the strict/centralizer inequality; \LemV Lemma V — what it buys; \QMOD (Q-MOD) — the reductive repair it is equivalent to.
\ThmD Theorem D — the modality cap, which ties the growth program to the same Borel-orbit geometry as the height conjecture.
\DegOpt (Deg-Opt) — the closed form for \operatorname {umod}(\mathfrak {n}_{c}), assembled from \Pfour (P4), \Pfive (P5) and \Psix (P6).

fr:mainmatter.html:p: How the macros work. Forester's \def binds its parameters as identifiers: in \def\umod[W]{\operatorname{umod}(\W)} the body must say \W, with the backslash. A bare W is ordinary text — the argument is silently discarded and the letter is printed instead. Expansion happens at build time, before math is serialized, so a macro is the only way to get a notation that the math renderer does not already know: an undefined control sequence reaches the renderer verbatim and fails there. Run ./forest/check-math.py to catch that.

Known collisions. Three glyphs currently carry two meanings apiece. The macros keep the two uses distinguishable in the source, so any of these can be resolved by editing one line here; none has been resolved unilaterally, because each is a notation decision.

html:ul.html:li: \kappa — the trace form \kappa (A, B) (\traceform) and the class count \kappa (G) (\classes).
F — the Frobenius F(M) (\Frob) and the growth functional F(c) (\Fof).
